history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 1464 (Shri Adishwar Temple, Bhavnagar / shri-adishwar-temple-palitana): both CSV rows describe the same principal Adinath shrine atop Shatrunjaya hill at Palitana, dedicated to Rishabhanatha, the first Tirthankara. Palitana-Shatrunjaya is the holiest pilgrimage centre of the Svetambara Jain community, with 800-900+ marble temples clustered behind fortified walls on the hilltop, reached by ~3,500-3,750 stone steps from Palitana town. The Adishvara temple, dated to the 16th century, has an ornamented spire and a main image of Rishabdev; the Chaumukh temple (1616) holds a four-faced Adinath image. Temples were built over ~900 years from the 11th century onward under patrons such as Kumarpal Solanki; early structures were destroyed by invading armies (13th-14th centuries, per tradition) and rebuilt from the 16th century. The complex is managed by the Anandji Kalyanji Trust. Palitana is a car-free, strictly vegetarian pilgrimage town. Coordinates are for the Shatrunjaya hilltop complex, approximate for the specific main shrine (verify exact position).

name: Adishwar Temple (Rishabhdev Temple)
town_description: Palitana is a temple town in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, about 55 km southwest of Bhavnagar city, at the foot of Shatrunjaya hill. It is one of the holiest pilgrimage centres of Jainism, hosting hundreds of marble Jain temples clustered on the hilltop, and draws pilgrims and visitors from across India and abroad, especially during the Kartik Purnima fair. It is a strictly vegetarian pilgrimage town served by its own railway terminus.

travel.road: Palitana lies on the Ahmedabad-Palitana road, approx. 50-55 km from Bhavnagar; buses and taxis available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather suits the long early-morning climb; the Kartik Purnima fair is the most important and most crowded period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hill temples are typically open from early morning (around 6:00 AM) to evening; the climb of ~3,500 steps takes 2-4 hours round trip — start early (verify current timings with the Anandji Kalyanji Trust). No photography inside some shrines (verify).
